entities.name: Cleobulina
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cleobulina, also known by her poetic appellation Eumetis (Εὔμητις, meaning 'prudent' or 'wise'), was an ancient Greek poet who flourished in the Archaic or early Classical period, likely around the 6th century BCE. The daughter of Cleobulus of Lindos, one of the revered Seven Sages of Greece, she emerged from an intellectual milieu that valued wisdom, gnomic verse, and rhetorical skill. Her significance lies in her rare status as one of the few named female intellectuals and poets from antiquity whose work, albeit fragmentarily, has survived, offering a unique feminine voice within the predominantly male-dominated literary landscape of ancient Greece.

Cleobulina's primary contribution was to the genre of riddles, a popular form of intellectual entertainment and didactic expression during ancient Greek symposia. Three riddles attributed to her are preserved through the writings of later authors like Athenaeus in his 'Deipnosophistae'. These riddles, characterized by their wit and clever wordplay, demonstrate her mastery of language and her keen observational skills. One famous example describes a measure of grain that grows when you take from it, referring to a sieve. Her ability to craft such intricate puzzles speaks to a sophisticated mind trained in the logical and linguistic intricacies central to Greek intellectual life.

The legacy of Cleobulina extends beyond the mere survival of a few riddles; it is in her very existence as a recognized female intellectual that she leaves a lasting mark. Her mention by ancient biographers and compilers like Diogenes Laërtius and Athenaeus ensures her place, however small, in the historical record of Greek literature and philosophy. She serves as a vital, if often overlooked, data point for understanding the intellectual capabilities and societal roles available to some women in certain privileged circles of the ancient Greek world, challenging simplistic narratives of universal female disenfranchisement.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Cleobulina holds significance as one of the extremely rare named female intellectuals from ancient Greece whose work survives, offering a unique perspective on the intellectual capabilities and contributions of women in antiquity. Her riddles showcase a sophisticated mastery of language and logic, contributing to the genre of gnomic poetry.
